      <title>Meeting of two lost souls: can Pochettino make it work at Manchester United? | Barney Ronay</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/11/mauricio-pochettino-manchester-united-old-trafford-manager</link>
      <description><p>Manager has been hurt by experiences at elite clubs but several players at Old Trafford could fit his playing style</p><p>Welcome, Mauricio, to the meat grinder. Or rather, welcome back. We’ve been expecting you. There is nothing surprising in the news Manchester United may be on the verge of appointing Mauricio Pochettino. United are always on the verge of appointing Pochettino. This is a club that has spent 13 years hiring and firing the same structurally doomed manager – same shellshocked eyes, same irresolvable macro-problems – and the last eight years almost but not quite doing this to Pochettino.</p><p>Well, maybe we’re finally here. Maybe he just needed to be broken enough to make it fit. And who knows, perhaps there is even a kind of accidental synergy here.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/11/mauricio-pochettino-manchester-united-old-trafford-manager">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Is No 10 still the best, or No 41? The myths and maths of Premier League shirt numbers</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/11/is-no-10-still-the-best-or-no-41-the-myths-and-maths-of-premier-league-shirt-numbers</link>
      <description><p>While No 9s still score the most goals and No 1s try to stop them, trends have changed since the introduction of squad numbers in the early 1990s</p><p>How much is a shirt number worth? It costs £8 if you want two digits added to the back of Arsenal’s 2026-27 home shirt, whereas Manchester City add on £16 for customisation, whether you want a name as well as a number or not.</p><p>That is cheap compared to what baseball players decide among themselves. Juan Soto bought Brett Baty a $92,000 (£69,000) car in exchange for getting his preferred number (22) when he joined the New York Mets last year. But that’s baseball, where they allow players to wear ‘0’. Anything goes.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/11/is-no-10-still-the-best-or-no-41-the-myths-and-maths-of-premier-league-shirt-numbers">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/premier-league-10-talking-points-weekend-action</link>
      <description><p>Delap’s talents resurface in style, Gómez delights Brighton with more fireworks, and hair-pulling confusion at Everton</p><p>It would have been very easy for Oliver Glasner to lose patience with Liam Delap. The forward is still only 23, yet the days when he was rattling in 12 in a Premier League season for Ipswich have come to seem a very long time ago (and his six games for Manchester City even longer). A season at Chelsea had left him bereft of confidence, an odd mix of diffidence and overaggression, devoid of composure in the box, arms flailing like a broken windmill. But the old gifts have not left him. Both goals on Saturday were the result of great muscular surges and if the first finish seemed essentially about hitting the ball as hard as possible on target, the second was a precise – and still powerful – finish in off the far post. After games such as this it’s possible to imagine him as England’s long-term replacement for Harry Kane. <strong>Jonathan Wilson</strong></p><p><em>Match report:</em> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/07/nottingham-forest-manchester-city-premier-league-match-report">Nottingham Forest 3-1 Manchester City</a></p><p><em>Match report:</em> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/08/manchester-united-aston-villa-premier-league-match-report">Manchester United 4-4 Aston Villa</a></p><p><em>Match report:</em> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/08/brighton-brentford-premier-league-match-report">Brighton 2-0 Brentford</a></p><p><em>Match report:</em> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/07/arsenal-hull-premier-league-match-report">Arsenal 1-0 Hull</a></p><p><em>Match report:</em> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/08/sunderland-chelsea-premier-league-match-report">Sunderland 1-0 Chelsea</a></p><p><em>Match report:</em> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/07/leeds-tottenham-premier-league-match-report">Leeds 1-0 Tottenham</a></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/09/premier-league-10-talking-points-weekend-action">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/07/arsenal-hull-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>As most Arsenal supporters would testify, patience is a virtue. They needed plenty during the 22-year wait <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/may/19/arsenal-premier-league-champions-manchester-city-bournemouth">to be crowned Premier League champions</a> and Mikel Arteta’s side certainly had to retain their composure as they tried to break down a dogged Hull side. They had not beaten Arsenal in 14 attempts since winning on their first visit to this ground in 2008. But with 20 minutes to play, there was still every chance that Sergej Jakirovic’s team could have pulled off one of the shocks of the season.</p><p>Arsenal had already been denied a penalty just before half-time for a shirt pull on Kai Havertz in the box a week after escaping <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/01/liverpool-arsenal-premier-league-match-report">the same crime against Liverpool</a> at Anfield, in a moment of controversy that could have been the major talking point from this match. Martin Ødegaard had other ideas and the Arsenal captain’s fifth goal of the season was enough to ensure they will go into the international break with a healthy lead over Manchester City. Enzo Maresca’s side are up next here in the league after the international break, with Arsenal having matched their record tally of 27 points from their opening 10 games. The signs look ominous for the rest, even if they were made to work for the points throughout by their opponents.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/07/arsenal-hull-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>
